inventory.observation: One construction, not separate panels: a horizontal boundary MN contains A left of B. A single vertical normal crosses the boundary at A and continues above and below it.

A1 is upper-left of A; an incoming arrow runs toward A. A2 is lower-right of A on the transmitted ray. B1 is upper-left of B; the second incoming arrow runs toward B through C. B2 is lower-right of B on its transmitted ray. Both incident rays are parallel; both transmitted rays are parallel. Transmitted rays bend toward the normal.

AC runs up-right from A to C, where C lies on the incident B1-B ray; AC is perpendicular to CB. DB runs up-right from lower point D to B; D lies on the transmitted A-A2 ray. DB is tangent to the A-centered wavelet at D and perpendicular to AD. ABC and ADB are right triangles sharing hypotenuse AB.

A large lower-medium circular arc is centered at A, crosses the lower normal, and reaches D with radius AD. Smaller lower-medium circular arcs have centers on AB and meet the sloping DB front. Their sizes decrease toward B. No circles are drawn in the upper medium.

Alpha is shown between the incident A1-A direction and the upper normal. Beta is shown between AD and the lower normal. These are normal-referenced incidence/refraction angles, not ray-to-interface angles. The additional source-only close-up confirms no duplicate alpha/beta labels or angle annotations at B: the curved marks below AB near B belong to secondary wavelets.

No lattice, table, subfigure letters, tick values, speeds, numerical angles, time values, frequency values, units, country symbols, portraits, or apparatus are present. M/N and A1/A2/B1/B2 are geometric endpoint labels, not cultural wording.
